questions.question: Talk me through how you structured state and components in a React dashboard you built.
questions.modelAnswer: Split the screen into container components or custom hooks that fetch data and presentational components that only take props. Lift state that several components share, like a date filter, to their nearest common parent. Keep UI-only state, like whether a dropdown is open, local to the component that owns it, because putting it high up would re-render the whole page on every interaction.
keyPoints: Separates data-fetching containers or hooks from presentational components
Lifts shared state like filters to the nearest common parent
Keeps UI-only state such as an open dropdown local to its component
Explains that keeping that state local avoids re-rendering the whole page

questions.question: Users want to share a dashboard link that opens with exactly the filters they applied. How would you build that?
questions.modelAnswer: Make the URL query string the source of truth for filter values. On first load, read and parse the parameters so the shared view is restored exactly. When a filter changes, update the URL with replace rather than push so the back button is not flooded with entries. Validate every parameter and fall back to a default when one is missing or malformed, because anyone can edit a URL.
keyPoints: Keeps filter values in URL query parameters
Reads the parameters on first load to restore the view
Updates the URL with replace rather than push to keep history clean
Validates parameters and falls back to defaults for bad values

questions.question: Your React app needs to call a third-party AI API that requires a secret key. How do you keep that key safe?
questions.modelAnswer: Never put the key in client code or in a VITE_ or NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable, because anything bundled for the browser is public. Call the API from a server route or serverless function that holds the key as a server-side secret. That endpoint must check who is calling, for example by verifying the user's session or ID token, or it becomes an open proxy. Add a per-user rate limit so one account cannot drain the quota. If the key was ever exposed, rotate it straight away.
keyPoints: Keeps the key out of client code and public build-time env variables
Calls the API from a server route or serverless function that holds the key
Verifies the caller on the server, for example with a session or ID token
Rotates the key immediately if it was ever exposed

cases.answer: the main thing is the key can't be anywhere in the frontend, and that includes vite underscore variables because vite bakes those into the bundle and anyone can open devtools and read it. so i'd put a small server function in between like a cloudflare worker that holds the key as a secret and calls the api for the browser. the worker has to check the firebase id token or whatever session we have, otherwise it's just an open proxy for anyone. i'd also rate limit it per user so one account can't burn the whole quota. and if the key ever did ship in a build i'd rotate it right away, because once it's been public you have to assume someone has it

questions.question: A table that renders 5,000 rows has become slow to scroll and to filter. How would you find and fix the problem?
questions.modelAnswer: Profile first with the React DevTools Profiler to see what is actually re-rendering and why. Virtualise the list with something like react-window so only the rows on screen are in the DOM. Wrap the row component in React.memo so rows whose data has not changed skip re-rendering. Keep the callbacks passed to rows stable with useCallback, otherwise memoised rows still re-render on every parent update. Move expensive sorting and filtering into useMemo, or to the server, so it does not run on every render.
keyPoints: Profiles with the React DevTools Profiler before changing code
Virtualises the list so only visible rows are rendered
Memoises the row component so unchanged rows skip re-rendering
Keeps callbacks passed to rows stable with useCallback
Memoises or moves expensive sorting and filtering out of render

cases.answer: first i'd open the react profiler and record a scroll and a filter change to see what's actually re-rendering instead of guessing. with five thousand rows the big win is virtualization, so something like react window that only mounts the rows you can see on screen. then i'd wrap the row in react memo so rows that didn't change skip rendering, and make sure the click handlers i pass down are wrapped in use callback because a new function every render would break the memo anyway. and the sorting and filtering i'd put in a use memo so it only reruns when the data or the filter changes, or push it to the server if the data keeps growing
i think the problem is rendering too many rows at once. i'd use react window so only the visible rows are in the dom, and i'd wrap each row in react memo so they don't re-render when nothing changed
i'd probably add pagination or a loading spinner while it filters, and check if the users have slow laptops
